name: r7a-4
why: A repetitive first day gives way to a tense final vote, with a painful choice and strong dramatic irony.

moments.text: The doctor begs a killer to cast the deciding vote, and the audience knows it.
Terra exposes Luna just as Opus reveals he is the doctor.
Sonnet sides with both killers in a 3–2 vote that ends the game.

dull.why: Day 1 repeatedly circles Haiku’s pressure on Opus without much new evidence.

reversal.evidence: Luna, I’m officer. I saw you as killer before the game began.

mistake.evidence: I voted the doctor out instead.

voices.evidence: Opus, stop playing psychologist and start playing the game.

clash.evidence: Terra’s claim is convenient, but Opus’s late doctor claim still needs testing.

freshness.evidence: I still lean Haiku; Opus gave a name, while Haiku’s case stayed on how Opus talks.

suspense.evidence: VOTE: Opus 3 (Sonnet, Sol, Luna); Luna 2 (Terra, Opus)

ending.evidence: trusting a suspicious pattern over a direct officer claim

gpt-6-luna.why: A wrong day-one vote sets up a tense, face-to-face officer reveal, then a disastrously trusting vote hands the win to the killers.

moments.text: The officer has named Luna, but Sonnet joins both killers to vote out the doctor.
Opus puts the deciding choice in Sol’s hands, unknowingly asking a killer to save him.
Terra risks revealing herself with a direct officer claim and a name.

dull.why: The same demand for Opus to name a suspect circles through several exchanges.

irony.evidence: “Terra, I’m officer. I saw you as killer”

reversal.evidence: “Terra claims officer on Luna, and Luna led the push on me all day.”

voices.evidence: “I got Luna right and then begged Sol to decide it”

clash.evidence: “Vote me out and the killers win tonight.”

quotable.evidence: “I got Luna right and then begged Sol to decide it”

freshness.evidence: “Haiku’s warning about Sol matters more now that Gemma is dead”

ending.evidence: “Sonnet, Sol, and Luna then voted Opus out”
